source_text: CYPRIANUS, LIBERALIS, CALDONIUS, JUNIUS, PRIMUS, CAECILIUS, POLYCARPUS, NICOMEDES, FELIX, MARRUTIUS, SUCCESSUS, LUCIANUS, HONORATUS, FORTUNATUS, VICTOR, DONATUS, LUCIUS, HERCULANUS, POMPONIUS, DEMETRIUS, QUINTUS, SATURNINUS, MARCUS, ALIUS SATURNINUS, ALIUS DONATUS, ROGATIANUS, SEDATUS, TERTULLUS, HORTENSIANUS, ITEM ALIUS SATURNIUS, SATTIUS, JANUARIO, SATURNINO, MAXIMO, VICTORI, ALIO VICTORI, CASSIO, PROCULO, MODIANO, CITTINO, GARGILIO, EUTYCIANO, ALIO GARGILIO, ALIO SATURNINO, NEMESIANO, NAMPULO, ANTONIANO, ROGATIANO, HONORATO FRATRIBUS SALUTEM. Cum simul in concilio essemus, fratres charissimi, legimus litteras vestras quas ad nos fecistis de iis qui apud haereticos et schismaticos baptizati videntur, an ad Ecclesiam catholicam, quae una et vera est, venientes baptizari debeant. De qua re quamquam et ipsi illic veritatem et firmitatem catholicae regulae teneatis, tamen quoniam consulendos nos pro communi dilectione existimastis, sententiam nostram non novam promimus, sed jampridem ab antecessoribus nostris statutam et a nobis observatam vobiscum pari consensione conjungimus, censentes scilicet et pro certo tenentes neminem foris baptizari extra Ecclesiam posse, cum sit Baptisma unum in sancta Ecclesia constitutum, et scriptum sit, Domino dicente: Me derelinquerunt fontem aquae vivae, et effoderunt sibi lacus detritos qui non possunt aquam portare. Et iterum divina Scriptura moneat et dicat: Ab aqua aliena abstinete, et fonte aquae alienae ne biberis. Oportet ergo mundari et sanctificari aquam prius a sacerdote, ut possit Baptismo suo peccata hominis qui baptizatur abluere, quia per Ezechielem prophetam Dominus dicit: Et aspergam super vos aquam mundam, et mundabimini ab omnibus immunditiis vestris, et ab omnibus simulacrhis vestris emundabo vos, et dabo vobis cor novum et spiritum novum dabo in vobis. Quomodo autem mundare et sanctificare aquam potest qui ipse immundus est et apud quem Spiritus sanctus non est cum Dominus dicat in Numeris: Et omnia quaecumque tetigerit immundus immunda erant. Aut quomodo baptizans dare alteri remissam peccatorum potest qui ipse sua peccata deponere extra Ecclesiam non potest?
pass_a_gloss: Cyprian and others to brothers, greeting. When we were together in council, dearest brothers, we read your letters which you made to us about those who seem to have been baptized among heretics and schismatics, whether they ought to be baptized when coming to the Catholic Church, which is one and true. About which matter, although you also hold the truth and firmness of the Catholic rule there, nevertheless since you thought we should be consulted for the sake of common love, we bring forth our opinion, not new, but already established by our predecessors and observed by us, joining with you in equal agreement, judging and holding for certain that no one can be baptized outside the Church, since there is one Baptism established in the holy Church, and it is written, the Lord saying: They have left me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water. And again, the divine Scripture warns and says: Keep away from foreign water, and do not drink from a foreign fountain. Therefore, the water must be purified and sanctified by a priest beforehand, so that it can wash away the sins of the person being baptized, because the Lord says through the prophet Ezekiel: And I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you, and I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you. But how can one who is unclean himself and with whom the Holy Spirit is not present purify and sanctify the water, when the Lord says in Numbers: And everything that the unclean person touches will be unclean? Or how can the one baptizing give remission of sins to another, who himself cannot put away his own sins outside the Church?

pass_b_english: Cyprian, Liberalis, Caldonius, Junius, Primus, Caecilius, Polycarpus, Nicomedes, Felix, Marrtius, Successus, Lucianus, Honoratus, Fortunatus, Victor, Donatus, Lucius, Herculanus, Pomponius, Demetrius, Quintus, Saturninus, Marcus, another Saturninus, another Donatus, Rogatianus, Sedatus, Tertullus, Hortensianus, likewise another Saturninus, Sattius, Januarius, Saturninus, Maximus, Victor, another Victor, Cassius, Proculus, Modianus, Cittinus, Gargilius, Eutyctanus, another Gargilius, another Saturninus, Nemesianus, Nampulus, Antonianus, Rogatianus, Honoratus—greetings to the brothers. While we were gathered in council, dearest brothers, we read the letters you sent us concerning those who appear to have been baptized among heretics and schismatics, asking whether they ought to be baptized upon coming to the Catholic Church, which is one and true. Although you yourselves already hold fast to the truth and firmness of the Catholic rule, you thought we should be consulted out of common love; so we set forth our opinion—not a new one, but one long established by our predecessors and observed by us—and join it with yours in full agreement. We judge and hold for certain that no one can be baptized outside the Church, since there is one Baptism constituted in the holy Church. It is written, the Lord saying: "They have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed out cisterns for themselves, broken cisterns that can hold no water" (Jeremiah 2:13). And again divine Scripture warns and says: "Keep away from foreign water, and do not drink from a foreign fountain." Therefore the water must first be purified and sanctified by a priest, so that by his Baptism it may wash away the sins of the one being baptized. For the Lord says through the prophet Ezekiel: "I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you. And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you" (Ezekiel 36:25-26). But how can one who is himself unclean, and in whom the Holy Spirit is not, purify and sanctify the water, when the Lord says in Numbers: "Everything that the unclean person touches shall be unclean"? Or how can the one who baptizes give another remission of sins, when he himself cannot put away his own sins outside the Church?
